title: The same repeat-unit formula does not mean the same enzyme substrate
original_forecast: Starch cleavage can occur without analogous cellulose cleavage. The two materials should not be treated as interchangeable simply because a formula parser sees the same repeat-unit atom counts.
original_limitations: Neither repeat-unit notation specifies chain length or crystallinity. Iodine is not a universal cellulose assay; use inventory changes for the cellulose control.
lock_qualification: Producer-reported manifest hash; artifact omits raw Cargo.lock bytes.

assessment.model_scope: Actual starch depletion/maltose formation and stoichiometric water debit distinguish cellulose, despite identical repeat-unit elemental composition. Reaction occurs at enzyme addition, not by a calibrated 30-minute kinetic law. Both iodine measurements read zero at405nm; unsupported KI mapping and particle glyph/speciation displays are not molecular inventory or a universal cellulose assay.
